questions.prompt: State what happens when the like poles of two magnets are brought together.
State the difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet.
questions.answer: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field; an induced magnet only becomes magnetic when placed in a magnetic field.

questions.prompt: State what happens to an induced magnet when it is removed from the magnetic field.
questions.answer: It loses most or all of its magnetism quickly.

questions.prompt: State the direction of a magnetic field line outside a bar magnet.
questions.answer: From the north pole to the south pole.

questions.prompt: State where the magnetic field of a bar magnet is strongest.
State what a compass needle's behaviour suggests about the Earth's core.
questions.answer: The Earth's core must be magnetic, since the compass needle points along the Earth's magnetic field.

questions.prompt: State what surrounds a wire when a current flows through it.
State the shape of wire that concentrates the magnetic field of a current into a strong, uniform field inside the coil.
State what an electromagnet is.
questions.answer: A solenoid with an iron core.

title: Force on a conductor and Fleming's left-hand rule

questions.prompt: Name the rule that shows the relative directions of force, current and magnetic field.
State the name of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
State the equation for the force on a conductor at right angles to a magnetic field.
questions.answer: Force = magnetic flux density × current × length (F = BIl).

questions.prompt: State what a coil of wire carrying a current in a magnetic field tends to do.
State the unit of magnetic flux density.
State what a loudspeaker converts variations in current into.
questions.answer: Pressure variations in sound waves (using the motor effect).

questions.prompt: Name the effect in which a conductor moving through a magnetic field induces a potential difference.
State what an induced current does to the change that causes it.
questions.answer: It generates a magnetic field that opposes the original change.

questions.prompt: State the condition for an induced potential difference to produce a current.
questions.answer: The conductor must be part of a complete circuit.

questions.prompt: State the type of current an alternator generates.
State the type of current a dynamo generates.
State the effect a moving-coil microphone uses to convert sound waves into variations in current.
State what a basic transformer consists of.
questions.answer: A primary coil and a secondary coil wound on an iron core.

questions.prompt: State why iron is used as the core of a transformer.
State whether the secondary potential difference is greater or less than the primary potential difference in a step-up transformer.
State the equation linking primary and secondary potential difference to the number of turns on each coil.
State the equation linking input and output power in an ideal (100% efficient) transformer.
Calculate the secondary potential difference of a transformer with 100 primary turns, 1000 secondary turns and a 230 V primary potential difference.
